title: Hull FC defeat Catalans Dragons with Jake Arthur's decisive kick
seoTitle: Hull FC edge Catalans Dragons with Jake Arthur kick
subtitle: Match marked by comeback, James Bell's injury, and praise for the Australian halfback
excerpt: In Perpignan, Hull FC came back against Catalans Dragons late thanks to Jake Arthur's field goal, while James Bell suffered a heavy clash.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: BBC, Total Rugby League, Hull Live
contentHtml:
The clash between Hull FC and Catalans Dragons, held at the Stade Gilbert Brutus, made headlines after ending 27-26 following a late field goal. The result flipped the narrative of the match, which was already trending in searches due to the comeback and the situation surrounding James Bell.

Hull FC's dramatic victory

Hull started the game on the front foot, scoring a try in the opening three minutes when James Bell broke through the line and passed to Logan Moy, who set up Aidan Sezer to convert. The team extended their lead in the 13th minute with a try from Arthur Romano, following a good play by Ethan O'Neill.

Catalans responded with tries from Charlie Staines, Kruise Leeming, Edenn Rogers-Smith, and Leo Darrelatour, turning the tide. In the second half, the Dragons reached 26-14, but Hull found strength in the final minutes. Harvie Hill scored a solo try and Sezer converted, leveling the match. Five minutes before the end, Jake Arthur, the Australian halfback, kicked a drop goal that secured the victory for the Black and Whites.

The decisive role of Jake Arthur

Jake Arthur received praise from Andy Last, Hull's interim coach, who highlighted the player's composure in scoring the decisive point. According to Last, the moment showed Arthur's quality to deliver a much-needed triumph for a team coming off a string of inconsistent results. Arthur himself was described as "outstanding" and "composed" in post-match evaluations.

James Bell's injury and its impact

During the second half, James Bell suffered a heavy high challenge, described as a possible "hip drop". The player received immediate treatment, had his knee immobilized, and was monitored by the medical staff. The incident was placed on report but did not result in an immediate sanction. Despite the concern, Bell remained on the field and contributed to the victory.

Hull's absences and physical challenges

In addition to Bell, Hull entered the clash without Will Pryce (anterior cruciate ligament injury), Zak Hardaker (knee), John Asiata (hamstring), Cade Cust (shoulder), Yusuf Aydin (knee), Connor Bailey (collarbone), Brad Fash (knee), Will Kirby (anterior cruciate ligament), and Joe Ward (anterior cruciate ligament). Hardaker and Bailey were in the process of recovery and could return in the coming weeks, while Cust was awaiting assessment after a shoulder injury.

Outlook for upcoming matches

With the victory, Hull FC records only their second win in ten Super League matches. The team returns to England for recovery and preparation ahead of their next clash against Warrington Wolves, while the coaching staff assesses the condition of Bell and the other absentees. Jake Arthur's performance could be decisive for the continuation of the campaign.

With information from BBC, Total Rugby League, Hull Live.
